svg.title: WebSocket over HTTP/1.1: secure setup, upgrade, duplex messages, and close
svg.desc: The browser and server establish TCP and TLS, then exchange an HTTP/1.1 Upgrade request and 101 Switching Protocols. The browser sends a JSON subscription, receives an update, sends command c7, and receives an application-defined acknowledgment that c7 committed. A clean close exchanges WebSocket Close frames before the transport closes. Network failure instead requires application reconnect, resubscription, replay, and duplicate-safe command handling. Extended CONNECT is a different handshake, not shown here.

g.text: WebSocket: setup, two-way messages, and close
Classic wss:// over HTTP/1.1; time flows downward
Browser / client
Server
1. Establish secure transport
2. Ask to switch protocols
3. Either side can send application messages
4. Graceful close in the HTTP/1.1 form
TCP + TLS handshakes (summarized)
GET /live; Upgrade: websocket
101 Switching Protocols
JSON message: subscribe to order o456
JSON message: order status changed
JSON command: cancel order; id: c7
Application acknowledgment: c7 committed
WebSocket Close frame, code 1000
WebSocket Close reply
TLS + TCP close (summarized)
Application acknowledgments are designed by your API, not WebSocket.
If the connection drops, reconnect, re-subscribe, and replay using retained history.
If c7 committed but its reply was lost, retry the same ID with server-side deduplication.
A successful send() or empty bufferedAmount does not mean the command committed.
HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 extended CONNECT uses a 2xx response and one stream, not this 101 upgrade.
Frames can fragment messages. Two-way messaging does not create independent application streams.
